senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. אור)to perforate; to be transparent, white, clear.
to make clear, evident. Mekh. Mishp., N’zikin, s. 13 (ref. to Deut. XXII, 17) מְחַוְּורִין … כשמלה they must make the fact as clear as a (white) sheet.
units: Gen. R. s. 98 (ref. to כבס, ib. XLIX, 11) שהוא מְחַוֵּור וכ׳ he will make clear to them the words of the Law; שהוא מח׳ להם טעיותיהם he will prove to them their errors; a. e.—Part. pass. מְחוּוָּר clear, proved, evident. Y. Shek. III, end, 47ᶜ מ׳ שבכולן the clearest of all the quoted Biblical evidences.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 47">Gen. R. s. 47</cite>, end; Y. Ab. Zar. I, 39ᵈ top <he>מ׳ שבכולן</he> the least doubtful of all. Y. Succ. V, beg. 55ᵃ <he>משם שאינו מח׳</he> because the use of the flute is not clearly stated in the Law. Y. Ter. II, 41ᶜ bot. <he>זה אחד … שהן מְחוּוָּרִין וכ׳</he> this is one of the three interpretations (of the Rabbis) which are clearly indicated in the Bible text. Y. Erub. III, 21ᵃ bot. <he>הגיעוך סוף … שאינן מח׳</he> thou must finally admit that the law of Sabbath limits finds no proof in the Biblical words. Y. Ber. II, 5ᵃ bot. <he>הגיעוך סוף מלאכות תפלה שאינן מח׳ מד״ת</he> ed. Lehm. (oth. ed. corr. acc.) thou must admit that for labors permitted or forbidden during prayer no support is to be found in &c.; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be made clear. Y. Keth. IV, 28ᶜ top (ref. to Deut. XXII, 17) עד שיִתְחַוְּורוּ וכ׳ the facts must be as clear &c., v. supra.
